A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from WASP to BEE. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v4 reports original zero-shot classification, regularized training, generated-image evaluations, and supplementary analyses in Tables 1–10 and Figure 4.

after.justification: v5 retains these empirical results and adds medical-text perturbations, embedding-model comparisons, and filtering and prompting ablations.

M1.justification: The renamed method retains the same Algorithm 1, linear probing, concept filtering, scoring, dynamic thresholding, and regularization objective. Appendix F documents existing filtering; additional encoder and filtering configurations are evaluated as variants. The inconsistent score definition introduced in Appendix J.3 is addressed under T1.

E1.justification: v5 adds MIMIC-CXR medical notes for finding/no-finding classification, substantially extending the evaluated domain beyond the four retained datasets. Appendix C also adds evaluations using ChatGPT-4o-generated images and naturally occurring photographs alongside the retained FLUX scenarios.

E2.justification: The main comparator sets remain unchanged, including B2T, SpLiCE, Lg, ERM, GroupDRO, and random-concept regularization in their corresponding experiments. Tables 9–10 add GPT-3.5 Turbo as an explicitly evaluated alternative to Llama-3.1 for BEE's concept-filtering component.

E3.justification: New protocols include appending 'chest examination' to clinical notes and measuring class recall, evaluating 40 ChatGPT-4o images split equally between two conditions, testing additional Waterbirds embedding configurations, and restricting prompts to positive or negative SCs. Existing benchmark protocols remain stated consistently; no separate new full-fine-tuning protocol is documented.

E4.justification: v5 adds checks of dependence on the image generator, natural-image validation, clinical-text perturbations, cross-embedding robustness, LLM-filter sensitivity, and positive-versus-negative prompting ablations. These substantially broaden the questions investigated beyond v4's retained thresholding, modality-gap, and loss-correlation analyses.

E5.justification: The uncertainty values in v4 Table 2 are retained in v5 Table 5. Neither version specifies their statistical meaning or run counts, and v5 introduces no seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or new repeated-run reporting practice.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark scores, classifier-transfer results, and concept-score lists match. Substantial new results include clinical recall changes of +2.1% for no finding and -2.2% for finding, 100% versus 50% accuracy in the separate ChatGPT-4o image experiment, and Waterbirds worst-group accuracies of 34.7% with negative-only prompts and 16.7% with positive-only prompts. These are additional conditions, not improvements over v4 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Appendix J.3 adds a binary positive/negative score-symmetry claim and proof. However, it uses a negative score of -b-min(-a,-b), whereas the retained main-text definition is -b, so the proof does not establish the claimed equality for that definition. The original equations and algorithm remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims of detecting named, learned SCs without counterexamples and working across image and text tasks remain. v5 explicitly foregrounds persistence after full fine-tuning and clinical false negatives, while reorganizing the contributions around diagnosis, transfer, and broad applicability.

C2.justification: New Section 5 and expanded Appendix E discuss dataset-induced versus foundation-model-induced shortcuts, justify linear probing, distinguish binary mitigation from multiclass detection, explain filtering risks and accuracy–fairness tradeoffs, and hypothesize transfer beyond classification while acknowledging that it was not tested. The original limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v5 adds the filtering prompt, response-validation rules, tokenization, stopword handling, WordNet processing, deduplication, and candidate counts. It also supplies temperature and GroupDRO parameter values, hardware and processing times, and code-access links where v4 promised public release. These substantially improve documentation without establishing changes to the existing implementation.

R1.justification: v5 extends the existing positioning with explicit comparisons to post-hoc and automatically constructed concept bottleneck models, plus references supporting linear probing, sparse-feature interpretation, and dataset generalization. The main distinction from data-based and error-based SC discovery is retained; much of the background is relocated.

P1.justification: The title and method name change, the abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, background material moves into the appendices, and the experiments are reordered. A dedicated discussion section and more structured appendix subsections substantially reshape the narrative.

P2.justification: v5 adds the compact embedding-comparison table, three filtering/prompting ablation tables, and a boxed filtering prompt. Existing tables are reordered and reformatted under the ICLR layout, with caption and color edits. All four figures retain their underlying visual content.

improvement.justification: The detailed filtering documentation and new component and image-source checks make the retained method easier to reproduce and assess. Clinical results also provide useful additional evidence. These gains are tempered by sparse protocol reporting for the medical and natural-image evaluations, the inconsistent negative-score proof in Appendix J.3, and the newly emphasized full-fine-tuning claim without a separately documented controlled experiment. The net quality improvement is therefore limited.
